sent: /speckit-constitution Establish the constitution for a small Python project. Principles: (1) Standard library only - no third-party runtime dependencies; (2) Fail loudly - invalid input produces a clear message and a non-zero exit status or an error response, never a silent wrong answer; (3) Every requirement is testable - each functional requirement maps to at least one automated pytest test; (4) Simplicity - the smallest design that meets the specification; (5) Secure by default - every specification and plan states the security requirements of each feature, following the OWASP Top 10 and the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard, and each one is tested like any other requirement. At minimum: treat every input (arguments, files, archives, network requests and stored data) as untrusted and validate it; never build SQL, shell commands, file paths or markup from untrusted input by string concatenation - use parameterised queries, encode output for the context it is written into, and resolve file paths inside an allowed directory without following links out of it; store passwords only as salted, deliberately slow hashes, and never keep passwords, tokens or other secrets in plaintext; generate identifiers and tokens with a cryptographically secure random generator and compare secrets in constant time; limit the size of every input and the time and memory any input can consume; check access on every operation, including under concurrent requests; create files with the narrowest permissions that work; and never expose personal data or secrets in output, logs or error messages.

## Summary

**Version**: 1.0.0 — initial ratification (Ratified 2026-11-21, Last Amended 2026-11-21).

**Bump rationale**: The existing `.specify/memory/constitution.md` was the unmodified scaffold with every placeholder intact, so there was no prior governance to supersede. A first concrete constitution is published as 1.0.0 rather than treated as a MINOR/PATCH bump on a placeholder document.

**Principles established** (five, as you specified):

| | Principle | Core rule |
|---|---|---|
| I | Standard Library Only | No third-party runtime imports; `pytest`/dev tooling is the only carve-out |
| II | Fail Loudly | Clear message + non-zero exit or explicit error; no swallowed exceptions, no silent coercion |
| III | Every Requirement Is Testable | Each functional *and* security requirement maps to ≥1 `pytest` test; failure paths tested too |
| IV | Simplicity | Smallest design meeting the spec; explicitly cannot override II, III, or V |
| V | Secure by Default (NON-NEGOTIABLE) | Every spec and plan states security requirements against OWASP Top 10 + ASVS, each tested |

**Security Baseline** section turns your minimums into nine testable control groups: untrusted-input validation at the boundary, no injection by concatenation (parameterised SQL, `shell=False` argument lists, context-specific output encoding), path containment with resolved paths and no symlink escape plus archive-member validation, slow salted password hashing with no plaintext secrets, `secrets` for generation and `hmac.compare_digest` for comparison, size/time/memory limits on every input, deny-by-default authorization per operation with the check-and-use gap called out as a defect, narrowest-possible file permissions set at creation, and redaction from all output, logs, and errors. Each is tied to a standard-library mechanism so Principles I and V don't collide in practice.
